chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nadhr from Yahya al-Halabi from Ayyub ibn 'Atiyyah said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) distributed the spoils of war, and Ali was allotted a piece of land. He dug a well in it, and water emerged from it, rising into the sky like the neck of a camel. He named it 'Ayn Yanbu'. The Basher came to give him glad tidings, saying: 'Give glad tidings to the Inheritor; it is a permanent charity, firmly established, for the pilgrims of the House of Allah and those passing through its way. It shall not be sold, nor given away as a gift, nor inherited. Whoever sells it or gives it away, upon him is the curse of Allah, the angels, and all people. Allah will not accept from him any deed or prayer.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan ibn Yahya, and it was also narrated by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn al-Sindi from Safwan from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who said: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) bequeathed this charity with the following words:

'This is what Musa ibn Ja'far gave in charity. He gave his land in such-and-such place, all of it, and its boundaries are such-and-such. He gave all of it in charity, including its palms, its land, its canal, its water, its edges, its rights, its share of the water, and every right belonging to it in elevated areas or lowlands, in width or length, in elbow-deep sections or open spaces, in irrigation channels or streams, in cultivated or uncultivated land. He gave all these rights in charity to his direct descendants, both men and women.'

The administrator shall distribute what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, brings forth from its produce, after what is sufficient for its maintenance and utilities, after thirty dates. He shall distribute among the poor of the village among the children of So-and-so: 'For the male is the share of two females.' If a woman from the daughters of So-and-so marries, she has no right in this charity until she returns to it unmarried. If she returns, she has the same share as the unmarried daughter of So-and-so.

And whoever from the children of So-and-so dies and leaves a child, his child inherits according to the share of his father: 'For the male is the share of two females,' as So-and-so stipulated among his direct children. And whoever from the children of So-and-so dies and leaves no child, his right returns to the people of the charity.

And the children of my daughters have no right in my charity unless their fathers are from my children. And no one has a right in my charity while my children, and the children of my children, and their descendants remain, as long as one of them remains. If they perish and none remain, then my charity goes to the children of my father from my mother, as long as one of them remains, according to what I stipulated among my children and their descendants.

When the children of my father from my mother perish, my charity goes to the children of my father and their descendants, as long as one of them remains, according to what I stipulated among my children and their descendants. When the children of my father perish and none remain, my charity goes to the first then the first, until Allah inherits it, who gave it, and He is the best of inheritors.

So-and-so gave this charity while he was sound of body, a permanent, firmly established, irrevocable charity, with no return and no reversal forever, seeking the Face of Allah and the Hereafter. It is not permissible for a believer 'who believes in Allah and the Last Day' to sell it, buy it, give it away, or alienate it, nor to change anything of what I described upon it, until Allah inherits 'the earth and whoever is on it.'

He made this charity under the administration of Ali and Ibrahim. If one of them perishes, al-Qasim enters with the remaining one. If one of them perishes, Ismail enters with the remaining one. If one of them perishes, al-Abbas enters with the remaining one. If one of them perishes, the eldest of my children enters with the remaining one. And if only one of my children remains, he is the one who administers it.'

key_terms.الْأَرْضَ وَ مَنْ عَلَيْهَا: The earth and whoever is on it (Quranic reference)
key_terms.لِلذَّكَرِ مِثْلُ حَظِّ الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ: For the male is the share of two females

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions and distribution rules for the permanent charity of Musa ibn Ja'far?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the permanent endowment (hab) of Musa ibn Ja'far, illustrating the Shia juristic distinction between the inalienable corpus of the land and the distributable produce (ghalla) for his descendants. It establishes a precise lineage of administration starting with his sons and transitioning to the eldest, reinforcing the concept of *sadaqah jariyah* as a perpetual act of worship that retains its spiritual merit even after the donor's death.
